Arista Networks gets BofA backing as 2027 growth outlook tops Street Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Arista Networks Inc (NYSE:ANET) drew higher estimates from Bank of America after its 2027 growth outlook topped Wall Street expectations, with the broker reiterating its "buy" rating and $240 price target.

Management forecast 39% revenue growth in 2027 against the Street's 28%, following third-quarter growth of 59%, above expectations of 44%.

That momentum is expected to continue into the fourth quarter, with growth guidance of 59% running nearly 15 percentage points above expectations, the broker said.

Bank of America raised its forecasts to reflect stronger demand, although peer valuation declines prompted a lower target multiple of 41 times estimated 2027 earnings, versus 49 previously.

Supporting Arista Networks' outlook, management expects AI revenue to double from $3.5 billion in 2026 to $7 billion in 2027, alongside 60% campus growth.

The broker also sees potential upside because it calculates that guidance implies only about 10% growth in enterprise switching.

Behind the AI forecast, Arista expects to participate in more than 10 gigawatts of new distributed AI capacity by the end of 2027, excluding existing data centers.

Using Dell'Oro assumptions, Bank of America estimates that capacity represents about $15 billion in underlying switching content.

Within that opportunity, Arista Networks expects connections between data centers, or "scale-across" applications, to account for more than one-third of AI revenue in 2027.

Management also expects operating margins near 49% in the fourth quarter and 2027, suggesting continued profitability despite AI investment, following a third-quarter margin of 49.1%.

Against that strong outlook, deferred revenue presents a caution, with sequential growth slowing from 15% to 10% before a 0.5% decline.

Product deferred revenue fell $86 million in the third quarter, although the broker said customer acceptance milestones may partly explain the slowdown.

Providing a counterweight, purchase commitments rose 18% sequentially, while management expects deferred revenue to remain at or above last year's $5.4 billion, supported by product launches and new applications.

Shares of Arista Networks rose about 6% on Wednesday.

Mid-cap banks are largely expected to benefit from fixed-asset repricing over the next 12 to 15 months, supporting continued earnings growth, with investors increasingly rewarding sustainable earnings improvement over quarterly beats, BofA Securities said in a Wednesday note.

In Q3, 70% of mid-cap banks beat earnings per share estimates, with 56% due to revenue, 59% on expenses, and 65% on lower credit costs, analysts said.

Popular (BPOP) and Columbia Banking System (COLB) are BofA's top picks as they have visible net interest margin support at attractive valuations.

Analysts said Texas Capital Bancshares (TCBI) was the "clearest winner" of the earnings cycle, adding that Central Bancompany (CBC) and Prosperity Bancshares (PB) shares outperformed amid increased confidence in repricing, cost savings, and forward earnings visibility.

BofA increased Central Bancompany's price objective to $36.50 from $33, Prosperity Bancshares' to $82 from $79, and Washington Trust Bancorp's (WASH) to $37 from $36. It lowered Associated Banc-Corp's (ASB) price objective to $32 from $34 and Commerce Bancshares' (CBSH) to $68 from $71.

title: Super Micro gets BofA upgrade to price target, but margins remain a concern

Super Micro gets BofA upgrade to price target, but margins remain a concern Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Super Micro Computer Inc (NASDAQ:SMCI) received a higher price target from Bank of America at $39 as stronger guidance failed to dispel concerns about margin sustainability.

Management raised its fiscal year 2027 revenue guidance to $72 billion to $82 billion and its gross margin outlook to 11.8%-12.2% following a strong fiscal first quarter.

Reflecting that outlook, the bank increased its fiscal year 2027 revenue and earnings per share forecasts to $81.2 billion and $6.34, respectively, from $79.6 billion and $5.31.

Super Micro Computer's target rose from $38, retaining a valuation of seven times estimated calendar year 2028 earnings per share, revised to $5.60 from $5.50.

Despite those increases, the broker questioned the durability of favorable non-AI server pricing and warned that a larger contribution from lower-margin AI deals would weigh on profitability.

Competition, component costs, and additional engineering support and services spending compound those pressures, with the bank expecting lower margins in the second half of fiscal year 2027.

Beyond profitability, substantial working capital needs underpin its forecast for continued negative free cash flow, while persistent material weaknesses in financial reporting controls add to its concerns.

Super Micro Computer also has high customer concentration in revenue and receivables, although management expressed confidence in its customers' credit quality, the bank said.

Balancing these risks, the broker highlighted strong AI demand and partnerships with Cisco, NetApp and Nutanix that support the company's efforts to reach more enterprise customers.

It also viewed capacity exceeding 8,000 racks monthly as a competitive advantage, with modular data center offerings potentially appealing to customers seeking faster deployment.

Funding remains a consideration, however, as management's lack of current capital-raising plans over the next 12 months depends on opportunities, with debt seemingly preferred over equity, the bank said.

Shares of Super Micro were down around 4.3% on Wednesday.

LendingTree, Inc. TREE announced plans to resume share repurchases in the fourth quarter of 2026, marking its first buyback activity since the first quarter of 2022. The decision reflects management's confidence in the company's improving financial position and its belief that TREE shares are attractively valued.

The announcement follows LendingTree's voluntary repayment of $60 million in long-term debt in the third quarter of 2026. Management highlighted debt reduction and share repurchases as its preferred capital allocation priorities, ahead of acquisitions and other investments.

TREE's Improving Balance Sheet Supports Buyback Plans

LendingTree has made considerable progress in strengthening its balance sheet. At the end of September 2026, the company had approximately $336 million in gross debt and $83 million in cash, translating into net leverage of 1.7X, down from 2.6X a year ago and 3.5X in the fourth quarter of 2024.

LendingTree, Inc.

Image Source: LendingTree, Inc.

The company is also approaching its stated objective of reducing net debt to $200 million. Its trailing 12-month levered free cash flow, adjusted for one-time litigation payments, reached approximately $100 million by the end of September 2026, underscoring its improving cash-generation capabilities.
Cash provided by operating activities increased to $76.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 from $56.6 million in the year-ago period. Such improvements provide LendingTree with greater flexibility to reward shareholders while continuing to strengthen its financial position.

Strong Revenue Growth Provides Additional Support

LendingTree's revenues for the first nine months of 2026 increased 23.4% year over year to $984.3 million from $797.6 million. Insurance revenues totaled $666.1 million, supported by strong carrier demand and continued expansion across its partner network. Home revenues reached $124.5 million, benefiting from healthy home equity lending demand, while Consumer revenues totaled $193.8 million.

The variable marketing margin increased to $281.8 million in the first nine months, while adjusted EBITDA reached $116.8 million, reflecting continued earnings growth. However, elevated marketing expenses pressured profitability, with the variable marketing margin declining as a percentage of revenues.

For 2026, LendingTree expects revenues of $1.30-$1.31 billion, variable marketing margin of $370-$375 million and adjusted EBITDA of $151-$153 million, indicating continued business expansion and earnings growth.

Investment bank Morgan Stanley (NYSE: $MS) has moved quickly to tokenize U.S. equities following the launch of new tokenization infrastructure on Wall Street.

Morgan Stanley is among the first banks to use the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's new tokenization infrastructure to tokenize popular U.S. stocks.

The tokenization of stocks is the process of converting shares of a company into digital tokens that are recorded on a blockchain or distributed ledger.

Digital versions of stocks can be traded around the clock and offer faster settlement times, according to advocates of the practice.

On social media, Morgan Stanley said that it has tokenized both U.S. stocks and government Treasury bonds, making it among the first Wall Street firms to do so.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation signed 20 participants to access its tokenization services, including Bank of America (NYSE: $BAC) and JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: $JPM).

Morgan Stanley is not alone in its efforts to quickly embrace the tokenization of stocks.

The New York Stock Exchange and its parent company Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: $ICE) plan to launch a tokenized trading platform in 2027.

Popular U.S. stocks that are being tokenized by Morgan Stanley and others include Apple (NASDAQ: $AAPL), Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA), and Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA).

MS stock has risen 14% over the last 12 months to trade at $186.09 U.S. per share.

MACAU, Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Studio City International Holdings Limited (NYSE: MSC) ("Studio City" or the "Company"), a world-class integrated resort located in Cotai, Macau, today reported its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Total operating revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were US$163.3 million, compared with US$182.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to softer performance in mass market operations leading to a decrease in revenue from casino contract and lower overall non-gaming revenues.

Studio City Casino generated gross gaming revenues of US$320.9 million and US$344.4 million for the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Mass market table games drop was US$846.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$942.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. Hold percentage was 34.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 33.1% in the third quarter of 2025.

Gaming machine handle for the third quarter of 2026 was US$892.9 million, compared with US$873.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Win rate was 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 3.7% in the third quarter of 2025.

Revenue from casino contract was US$66.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$77.3 million for the third quarter of 2025. Revenue from casino contract is net of gaming taxes and the costs incurred in connection with the on-going operation of the Studio City Casino which are deducted by Melco Resorts (Macau) Limited, the gaming operator of the Studio City Casino (the "Gaming Operator").

Total gaming taxes and the costs incurred in connection with the on-going operation of the Studio City Casino deducted from gross gaming revenues were US$254.0 million and US$267.2 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Total non-gaming revenues at Studio City for the third quarter of 2026 were US$96.4 million, compared with US$105.2 million for the third quarter of 2025.

Operating income for the third quarter of 2026 was US$14.7 million, compared with US$23.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Studio City's Adjusted EBITDA(1) was US$65.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$78.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The change was mainly attributable to lower revenue from casino contract and softer performance in non-gaming operations.

Net loss attributable to Studio City International Holdings Limited for the third quarter of 2026 was US$13.1 million, or US$0.07 per American depositary share ("ADS"), compared with US$18.6 million, or US$0.10 per ADS, in the third quarter of 2025. The net loss attributable to participation interest was US$1.2 million and US$1.7 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

title: Nike Got a $50 Target and a $24 Target the Same Day. Its Gross Margin Explains Why
detail:
Nike Got a $50 Target and a $24 Target the Same Day. Its Gross Margin Explains Why

Trading disclosure
Nike Got a $50 Target and a $24 Target the Same Day. Its Gross Margin Explains Why ©ValentynVolkov from Getty Images, Artem Varnitsin via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bank of America cut its Nike target to $24 on Oct. 2, keeping its Underperform rating, the same day BTIG cut its Buy-rated target to $50. Barclays raised its target to $45 on Oct. 22, and Bernstein reiterated its $45 Outperform call on Nov. 3.

Nike's gross margin rose 60 basis points to 42.8% in the quarter to Aug. 31. It's the first year-on-year gain in seven quarters that didn't come from a tariff recovery.

BTIG and Bank of America are just 15 cents apart on fiscal 2028 EPS. The gap is the multiple: about 30x for BTIG, 16x for Bank of America.

The quarter backs the Buy side, but at 30x forward earnings with revenue still falling, Nike needs its Dec. 17 report to show the margin rising again.

On Oct. 2, the day after its first-quarter report, two Wall Street firms looked at the same Nike (NKE:NYSE) quarter and ended up $26 a share apart. BTIG cut its target to $50 from $55 and kept its Buy rating, while Bank of America cut its target to $24 from $30 and kept its Underperform rating. Both firms reaffirmed those targets the week of Oct. 19, when Barclays raised its target to $45 from $37 and kept its Overweight rating.

NKE Stock Price: Year-to-date (TIKR)

The stock is up 13.6% in the past month and still down 38% in 2026.

Bank of America's own math says the gap is less about earnings than about the multiple. For me, gross margin is the best test of which multiple Nike deserves, and it just turned.

Bank of America's $24 Is a Multiple Call

Analysts expect Nike's normalized EPS to fall again in fiscal 2027 (the year to May 2027), then rise in fiscal 2028:

NKE Normalized EPS, Actual and Estimates: Fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Even that rebound only gets Nike back to about fiscal 2026's $1.58, and to less than half of fiscal 2024's $3.95.

Bank of America's $24 is 16 times its own fiscal 2028 earnings estimate, according to TheStreet, which works out to about $1.50 a share. BTIG's $50 is about 30x its fiscal 2028 estimate of $1.65. Those two estimates sit on either side of the $1.56 consensus, just 15 cents apart. The real split is the multiple: BTIG will pay nearly twice as much as Bank of America for about the same recovery.

Nike guides fiscal 2027 revenue down by a high-single-digit percentage, so margins have to drive that recovery. Analysts see Nike's EBIT margin rising from 5.7% in fiscal 2027 to 7.0% in fiscal 2028.

BofA lowered its price target on Axsome to $264 from $276 but maintained a 'Buy' rating, representing an 85% upside potential.

TD Cowen analyst Joseph Thome reiterated a 'Buy' rating with a $135 price target, calling shares 'significantly undervalued.'

Axsome reported a 52% surge in Q3 revenue to $259.7 million, above estimates of $249.2 million, according to Fiscal.ai

Shares of Axsome Therapeutics (AXSM) have declined nearly 20% over the past month, but Wall Street believes the selloff may be excessive despite concerns surrounding the company's Alzheimer's disease agitation treatment launch.

AXSM stock was up 5% at the time of writing, having fallen to a 52-week low in the previous session.

BofA Still Sees Significant Upside

BofA lowered its price target on Axsome to $264 from $276 but maintained a 'Buy' rating, according to The Fly. The updated price target still implies a roughly 85% upside from current levels.

The firm said that while Axsome's third-quarter (Q3) results were largely in line with expectations, investors remain concerned about the pace of the Alzheimer's agitation treatment launch and whether the company can meet full-year 2027 estimates.

BofA said concerns about the slower-than-expected adoption of Axsome's Alzheimer's agitation treatment and its ability to meet full-year 2027 revenue estimates have weighed on shares, but the firm believes the selloff is excessive given the drug's long-term growth potential.

Meanwhile, Baird lowered its price target on Axsome to $220 from $246 and keeps an Outperform rating on the shares.

Axsome's Q3 Revenue Growth Driven By Auvelity Sales

Axsome reported a 52% surge in third-quarter (Q3) revenue to $259.7 million, above estimates of $249.2 million, according to Fiscal.ai. Auvelity drove the growth, with sales up 53% to $207.6 million.

The company reported a loss of $0.25 per share, beating consensus estimates of a $0.64 per-share loss. Axsome ended September with $313.9 million in cash and expects its existing funds to support operations until it becomes cash-flow positive.

Auvelity, an oral medication, was originally approved in 2022 to treat major depressive disorder. In April, 2026, the FDA approved Auvelity for agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia. Axsome launched the treatment for this new use in June 2026.
